Fuck you. Digitizing the books we have is one of the smartest things we can do. Or have you never heard of the Library of Alexandria?

I am of two minds on the issue. Authors deserve to be paid for their work, so I might be on board with waiting till the original author passes to make the books available online for free. But as you point out. It should be seen as a duty of humanity to collect our works in a way that we can best preserve them.

I'm not even necessarily saying they need to be made free to the public, though that is obviously ideal. I have no problem with artists getting paid but I think they should be willing to at least allow Google to digitize them (maybe let people buy the digital versions, pass profits to authors) for the sake of longevity. We have lost countless centuries worth of knowledge over time to physical destruction and having our most treasured pieces of literature distributed across multiple mediums makes that infinitely less likely.

My major concern would be that it is no better to have one company do the archival work for humanity than it is to use an unstable medium for saving those works. Google is not an altruistic organization. Rather it is an opportunistic one. So I remain of two minds on the topic. I want to say the larger part of me wants to see knowledge recorded at whatever cost.
